column3: Registering distinct CDP browser endpoints yields distinct persistent UUIDs and unused Jelly dessert aliases.
Two registered browser_ids can navigate independent pages without sharing target labels, state or download artifacts.
An operator can select native, dedicated-subnet or address-based CDP access; the connection mode is reported accurately.
When a chosen sandbox/restriction combination fails, Jelly diagnoses failure and suggests options without silently changing the requested settings.
Publishing CDP on a requested bind IP:port is an opt-in choice; defaults do not publish host ports and exposure is reported.
Each remote browser applies its selected remote-only, shared-volume or HTTP(S) transfer policy and reports correct artifact availability.
